nodes.label: The engine core stays pure
nodes.rationale: Pure functions over value objects with no I/O, network, DB or clock make 524 tests run in ~4s with no fixtures and keep a native client possible. Persistence and HTTP live at the edges and call into the engine, never the reverse.

nodes.label: Enums are shared, never forked
nodes.rationale: Equipment and MovementPattern are defined in hibrid.models and re-exported by hibrid.user.enums; two divergent copies would break every join between a routine and a user's history. Weekday gets the same treatment when the weekly plan lands.

nodes.label: Two model styles (dataclasses vs pydantic)
nodes.rationale: hibrid.models uses stdlib dataclasses (internal, trusted YAML, hot path); hibrid.user and hibrid.api use pydantic v2 at untrusted boundaries where extra='forbid' makes a renamed device field raise at ingestion instead of vanishing.

nodes.label: Account key resolves to identity
nodes.rationale: The device holds one secret; the server resolves it to account_id and fills user_id itself. Account.account_id IS UserProfile.user_id. Credentials are a collection not a column, keeping the upgrade path open.

nodes.label: Each objective chooses its variation invariant
nodes.norm_label: each objective chooses its variation invariant
nodes.rationale: LOAD_VOLUME holds sets*reps*weight (hypertrophy, endurance); INTENSITY pins load at reference (strength). Solving load from a volume target under strength preserves arithmetic but destroys the training. The invariant is a property of the objective, never a caller parameter.

nodes.label: Variation vs progression tension
nodes.rationale: Adaptation requires repetition: strength is a movement-specific motor skill measurable only on a stable history. Variation keeps training engaging while progression needs stability. VariationPolicy is where that line lives.

nodes.label: Four-tier input resolution
nodes.community_name: Health data stays on the device
nodes.rationale: Inviolable (health) > hard constraint (equipment, time) > training correctness (objective invariant, substitution ceiling) > soft preference (dislikes, novelty) > adaptive (readiness, intent, load). A lower tier can never veto a higher one.

nodes.label: Health data stays on the device
nodes.community_name: Health data stays on the device
nodes.norm_label: health data stays on the device
nodes.rationale: Special-category health data (GDPR Art. 9) plus Apple/Google store terms carry obligations an order of magnitude heavier than ordinary personal data; keeping the health bucket off the server keeps all of it off the company. Health/biometrics are request-scoped inputs the engine forgets.

nodes.community_name: Re-rolling a block drops the adaptive...
nodes.norm_label: re-rolling a block drops the adaptive tier
nodes.rationale: A generated block's weight already embodies load_multiplier, so re-solving with the same context applies difficulty/readiness/taper twice; without_adaptive_load neutralises them so a challenging session does not climb 15% per re-roll. Inviolable and hard tiers stay untouched.
